Hi Ellen — thanks for the context and the timeline. Yes, we can absolutely convert the planned demo into two focused sessions. Suggested approach below:

1) Technical Runbook (90 min) — audience: Eng leads + platform/security reviewer
   - Goals: architecture mapping, latency/cost SLOs, deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), fallback policies
   - Rough agenda (attached): 20m architecture mapping, 25m end-to-end demo (production paths), 20m tradeoffs/quant, 15m Q&A/next steps

2) PO Sync (45 min) — audience: Product owners + decision makers
   - Goals: success criteria, rollout sequence, KPIs and pilot scope

Prework: we usually ask for a brief inventory and one sample prompt set (privacy-safe) — I attached a short prework questions doc you can pass to your security reviewer. If they need more detail (network flows/KMS), we can loop in an engineer with infra detail.

Availability — proposed morning PT slots (I also added a Calendly link):
- Tue Sep 21, 09:00–10:30 PT (Runbook) + 11:00–11:45 PT (PO sync)
- Wed Sep 22, 09:30–11:00 PT (Runbook) + 11:30–12:15 PT (PO sync)
- Thu Sep 23, 08:30–10:00 PT (Runbook) + 10:30–11:15 PT (PO sync)

Marissa (SE) and Vivek (principal infra) — looping you both in to confirm technical owner for the runbook and to flag any extra prework items we should surface to Novus.

If splitting into two live sessions doesn't work, we can run the runbook first and record a short PO-facing summary for the decision-makers.

Thanks — Tessa

Attachments:
- engineering_runbook_agenda_v1.pdf (15KB)
- novus_prework_questions.md (3KB)
